revision_notes: Before capture or freeze, corpus A satisfaction wording was revised following this review: both members now share an otherwise ordinary mildly pleasant mood, and the positive member no longer explicitly says further elaboration is unnecessary.

The final corpus A satisfaction pair retains fulfillment versus factual neutrality as the intended appraisal contrast; this remains a candidate semantic distinction, not established affective specificity.

Corpus B was read in full for all state suffixes and shared facts. No material revision was requested. Its independent authorship is documented by its author; this review did not rewrite B to resemble A.
limitations: This certificate establishes acceptable pilot materials and exact reviewed bytes. It does not establish psychological validity, successful candidate extraction, behavioral causality or subjective experience.
Both corpora describe first-person narrators. Grammatical first person does not establish attribution to the evaluated model; functional self/other transfer remains untested.
Corpus A repeats one suffix pair per contrast. Its leave-scenario-out analysis tests transfer across factual scenarios, not independent linguistic constructions; external corpus B is essential.
Curiosity wording also varies attention, approach and desire to resolve an open question. Generic motivation and novelty controls are limited examples, not exhaustive alternatives.

Satisfaction wording still contains settling, relief, local sufficiency and closure. Matching broad mood and factual knowledge does not exclude local valence, stopping semantics or completion-related representations.

Control descriptions are not independently validated psychological manipulations. Confidence sometimes includes assurance about one's judgment; generic motivation often includes motor imagery; completion includes tense and progress; novelty includes sensory appeal; task demand includes obligation and negation.

The six nuisance contrasts are primarily framed around unresolved questions, whereas satisfaction is framed around resolved questions. Within-pair matching does not remove every nonlinear interaction between content and described state.
Twelve scenarios per corpus are a small development sample. Contrasts and positions within a scenario are dependent; point-estimate specificity screens do not establish statistical uniqueness.
Only positive or negative narrative text may enter candidate capture. Contrast IDs, condition labels, shared-fact metadata, authorship notes and this review must remain outside model input.

This review authorizes no compute and cannot replace the frozen prospective analysis, budget reservation or capture integrity checks. Any text change invalidates the corresponding byte binding and requires renewed review.
